answer.reason: The verses tell Hannah's own story: her prayer and vow for a son, and bringing him to the LORD's house after he was weaned.

clauses.english: vowed to give a son to the LORD if he would look on her affliction
clauses.quote: if thou wilt indeed look on the affliction of thine handmaid

clauses.english: brought the weaned child Samuel to the house of the LORD in Shiloh
clauses.quote: brought him unto the house of the LORD in Shiloh

clauses.english: was visited by the LORD and bore three more sons and two daughters
clauses.quote: the LORD visited Hannah, so that she conceived, and bare three sons and two daughters

doubts: Her bearing Samuel is already in the summary (mother of Samuel), so it is not a clause.
Her song of praise in 1SA 2:1 is a prayer and was left out as not a distinct event.
